name: Priscilla
overview: Priscilla is a female biblical figure known primarily as the wife of Aquila, as recorded in Acts 18:2. No tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided about her background. Her identity is closely tied to her partnership with Aquila in the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: Priscilla, also referred to as Prisca, is the proper name given to this individual in Scripture. There is no specific meaning or divine origin noted for her names in the biblical text provided.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Priscilla is the wife of Aquila. Beyond this marital relationship, no other family connections are documented in the given information.
scriptureSignificance: Priscilla's significance in the New Testament arises from her role alongside her husband Aquila in the early church. Mentioned in both Acts and Romans, she is part of a Christian couple who contributed to the ministry and fellowship of the believers. Her presence in these passages highlights the active involvement of women in the foundational period of the church.
